name: [R23] Repeated OAuth UserInfo failures / oversized Authorization header consistent with F5 BIG-IP APM CVE-2026-94127
message:
Indicators of CVE-2026-94127, a heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122) in F5 BIG-IP APM's OAuth UserInfo handler, CVSS 9.8, patched by F5 2026-09-22. Pre-auth RCE when APM is configured as an OAuth Authorization Server with an access policy and OAuth profile on the virtual server. F5 confirmed active exploitation; CISA KEV 2026-09-22 (federal deadline 2026-09-25). JPCERT/CC issued JPCERT-AT-2026-0028 citing watchTowr Labs' exploitation write-up.

Built directly from F5's and JPCERT/CC's own published compromise-detection guidance (K000162605, AT-2026-0028): repeated OAuth UserInfo request failures (apm log ID 01990004) from one source, especially in a short window, correlate with heap-grooming attempts; an oversized Authorization header against the UserInfo endpoint is the proximate exploitation vector. Neither is proof alone -- F5's own guidance treats the log-ID pattern as a lead needing further checks (tmctl OAuth failure stats, /var/log/audit correlation, a TMM core-file check), not confirmed compromise.

Confirm any hit against the exact installed BIG-IP APM version (vulnerable: 21.1.0; 17.5.0-17.5.1; 17.1.0-17.1.3) via scripts/f5_bigip_apm_check.py, and check for a TMM core file or /etc/bigstart/scripts/tmm.finish tampering before escalating.

cases.name: OAuth UserInfo failure burst from one source (threshold: tune to >=10 in your SIEM, per F5's own guidance)
Oversized Authorization header to UserInfo endpoint observed
